races.title: State House, District 96
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Danielle Duggar

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Republican elected to Alabama House District 96 in 2026, after defeating incumbent Matt Simpson in the primary. Works as a legislative analyst/advocacy associate for a national nonprofit and teaches ACT English and reading prep. Holds a BA (UMGC) and an MA in American History (Norwich). Has held no prior office.

endorsements.text: Alabama Farmers Federation (listed on her campaign site)
Gun Owners of America and National Association for Gun Rights (listed on her campaign site)
Alabama Republican Assembly, Health Freedom Alabama, Orange Beach Mayor Tony Kennon and other groups (listed on her campaign site)
Recommended by the Sway voting group (Mary Talley Bowden, MD) under "Pull mRNA Shots Off the Market"

cands.gaps: We could not find where Danielle Duggar was born or raised, or the year she moved to Alabama. We found no record of her holding office before 2026, so there are no past actions in office to report. We found no stated positions from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on out-of-state or foreign land buyers, immigration or H-1B, or police pay and public-order laws. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey, so her policy statements come from her campaign website and a 2022 survey. Her website says she opposes tax increases but does not mention homestead taxes specifically.

second-amendment.evidence: Says she will stand against any attempt to infringe gun rights and criticizes the 2025 passage of SB 116 and SB 119 as restrictions on the Second Amendment.

pro-life.evidence: Says she is committed to the sanctity of human life for the unborn and the elderly.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: In her 2022 Ballotpedia survey she said she believes in school choice.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Says growth should serve communities, with planning that supports farms and protects natural resources, not just more development for profit.

cands.name: Terri Osborne

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Terri Osborne is a geologist and Daphne resident of about 30 years. She was the Democratic nominee for Alabama House District 96 in 2026 and has a bachelor's and a graduate degree from the University of Alabama. She has not held public office.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as recommended by the voter guides Tabitha's List (Sway voting group by Tabitha Isner) and Unburdening The Ballot (Sway voting group by Tevin Davis).

cands.gaps: We could not confirm where Terri Osborne was born or raised, or the year she moved to Alabama. Her high school's location was not stated in the pages we read. She has held no public office, so there is no record of actions in office. We found no stated position from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on out-of-state or institutional land buyers, immigration or H-1B, policing, or teacher pay.

local.label: Roots 55: She describes herself as a 30-year Daphne resident and earned University of Alabama degrees in 1985 and 1988, but her birthplace and upbringing are not documented, so the score reflects adult residency of roughly 30 years. · Money: 21% of money from District 96 ZIP codes

qual.label: Geology is not directly related to lawmaking or budgeting, and no prior legislative or local elected service was found.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Said she opposes Alabama's voucher program and does not want tax dollars used for religious education, citing first-year data that most voucher money went to students already in private school or homeschooling.

pro-life.evidence: Said medical decisions including reproductive care, IVF, abortion and contraception belong to women and their doctors, and called for codifying these protections in federal law.

second-amendment.evidence: Listed implementing gun safety reforms among her policy interests, with the aim of making deaths of minors from guns rare.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Said a proposed large solar facility in Stockton, just outside District 96, threatens wetlands and the Tensaw River and Mobile Bay watershed, and that solar should be sited on flat, former agricultural land rather than at the expense of fragile ecosystems.
